summary: For every ES word γ=[[cu−1,p],[c,cB−1]] (c=4C) the fixed form is [c, c(B−u), −p] of disc (a+d)²−4 = (c(u+B)−2)²−4, so p always sits on the river edge adjacent to the value c with edge label ≡0 mod c — a tautological location; computed all words/rivers for p<500 (no word at p=409 as expected), and the discriminant depends only on c(u+B), shared across many p. This is exactly the X-certificate ambiguous form [−t,tβ,p] of disc T²−4 in WINDMILL_REDUCTION §5.2/§8 (reduces to the e/t-slice problem) plus §10 Prop 10.3 (form-class mechanisms see only the genus shadow).

The fixed-C generating function Σ_{u,B≥1} q^{4CuB−u−B} is the degenerate (split, a=c=0) Hecke-type double sum; METAPLECTIC_ES Thm K (via Kronecker's double-series identity) already writes positive-cone minus partner-cone as the Kronecker theta quotient q^{t−2}(Q;Q)²θ(X²)/θ(X)² (odd-character divisor sums, holomorphic Jacobi-form data, no mock part) and the even part as even-character divisor sums. BRAINSTORM/z39_square_discriminant_shadow.md and z39_kronecker_levels.md record that no Appell–Lerch/mock part appears (Hickerson–Mortenson degenerate case); the 'two-sign' count N₋−N₊ is exactly D⁻−D⁺ of (K1′).

Setting up the first step shows the 𝔽_p formulation degenerates: every Type II certificate has ff′ = 1 + 4c²dp ≡ 1 (mod p), so all certificate points lie on the single curve xy = 1 in 𝔽_p² for every (c,d) — the (c,d)-family is only visible over ℤ, where the curves are hyperbolas xy = 1+4c²dp and Stevens–de Zeeuw/Rudnev (verified: arXiv:1609.06284) give only incidence UPPER bounds. That is exactly gon_incidence_kloosterman.md §3 (c2): incidence bounds bound f(p) from above, existence needs lower bounds that come only from identities (B1); a second-moment use only reproduces average-over-p results.

Computed the cheapest integer parity count, R(p)/2 = #unordered (★) triples mod 2, for the 147 primes p≡1 (4) < 2000: 75 odd / 72 even, and R=0 at 409, 577 — no parity law (matches WINDMILL_REDUCTION §3.3 '~50/50'). Chevalley–Warning/Ax–Katz count 𝔽_q-points, i.e. local data, which hold equally at odd squares (T1) — already recorded in B2_ACROSS_FIELDS §5 M5, BRAINSTORM/invol_topological.md (G-L/CW paragraph) and polynomial_method.md (b3: zero-sum methods certify +1, ES needs −1); no F₂-encoding of the integer certificate set was found that escapes this.

SINGLE_P_COUNT §6 Prop 6.1 (summary BRAINSTORM/z30_sl2_double_coset.md) already wrote R(p) as the count of −γ∈Γ₁(c) with b(γ)=p, c=4C its own lower-left entry: there is one Γ_∞-double coset per level c, and selecting the class a≡d≡−1 needs all frequencies mod c, so inside a coset b=p is just the divisor problem of cp+1; the transposed picture has a single level p with a height-dependent target. Neither yields Σ_c S(m,n;c) with fixed (m,n) over a long c-range, so Kuznetsov/Proskurin main terms enter only after averaging over p ((D)32, B6); the item's first step is exactly this computation.

Computed the image mod q of all length-3 ES words T^u(−1 0; c −1)T^B = [[cu−1,(cu−1)B−u],[c,cB−1]] (4|c when 4|q) in SL₂(ℤ/q) for q ≤ 40 and q ∈ {48,60,64,97,120}: for prime q it covers ≈ 1−1/q of SL₂ (all c invertible), with the 4|c restriction ≈ 1/(2·4)-type fractions, and every unit b-entry (= p mod q) is hit for every q. So the short-word image mod q is already locally full with no expansion needed — the obstruction is integral (b = p exactly, entries in the word range), which is local-to-global data that Bourgain–Gamburd/Varjú (long-word equidistribution mod q) cannot see and which holds equally at odd squares (T1/B5).

Instead of a blind polynomial ansatz I tested the obstruction for identities in (a,b) with p = a²+b²: by Hilbert 90, N(α)=s² ⇔ α = s·δ²/N(δ), so locally every coset (a0,b0) mod M whose norm is a unit square mod M (exactly the Mordell-hard situation) contains odd-square-norm points; CERTIFIED by enumeration for M = 40 (128/128 cosets) and M = 120 (512/512) with m coprime to M. Hence a 2-variable identity valid on such a coset is evaluated at some a²+b² = m² and meets T1 (Type I/II at odd squares impossible), which is the 'two-variable Theorem M / square-mimicking point' left open in BRAINSTORM/nonab_frobenius_redei.md §3 (E2 channel); the only unchecked step is that the identity's solution stays Type I/II (coprimality) at generic such m², which fails only if (a²+b²) divides some X_i.

Listed as untried, but WINDMILL_REDUCTION §10 already does exactly this: a certificate (4uC−1)(4BC−1) = 4Cp+1 is the balanced Bhargava triple / 2×2×2 cube with Q₁=[m,2,m″] of disc −4tp (Lemma 10.1), the divisor hypercube embeds injectively in Cl(−4tp) (10.2, PROVED all p,t), and Prop 10.3 proves every mechanism factoring through form/cube classes and their S₃⋉(ℤ/2)³ symmetries sees m ≡ −1 (mod t) only via its genus shadow; Remark 10.4 identifies ray class groups mod t as the only class-type escape, which restates B2. No new composition law on (★) triples emerges.

Short proof attempt: for a prime q ∤ 2m, 'q ≡ −1 (mod m)' is equivalent to 'q is a primitive divisor of U_m(P,Q) for some (P,Q) with (D/q) = −1' (choose α/β of order m in the norm-1 torus of 𝔽_{q²}), so p-dependent Lucas sequences only restate the prime-certificate subcase of B2, while BHV guarantee a primitive divisor of U_m itself, never of 4Cp+1; tying them needs U_{4C}(P,Q) | 4Cp+1, a Thue-type coincidence of probability ~|α|^{−4C}. BRAINSTORM/y3_lucas_dickson_trace.md already records that Lucas ranks encode 4cd | h+1 but not the residue condition and that primitive divisors ≡ −1 (mod 4cd) divide U_{4cd}, not p+4c²d (B2), plus Prop G (Galois-descent collapse).

BRAINSTORM/z45_interlacing_stable.md already treats Lee–Yang/real stability/interlacing for exactly these divisor-sector polynomials, with exact computations at the hard primes and odd squares: MSS signings are all the same polynomial (gauge-removable), the class-extraction operator Π_{−1} destroys stability (e.g. at 2521 the only occupied level gives z²+z⁴; ∏(1+z_i) ↦ e₁+e₃), and the certificate-filtered real-rooted polynomial has a nonzero root iff the edge already exists. The item's first step (zeros of P_p(z)=Σ z^{u+B+C}) is weaker than this: P_p ≡ 0 exactly when R(p)=0, so its zero geometry cannot force existence; nothing beyond the memo.

Chen–Stein per se is not in the repo, but its ingredients (dependency neighbourhood mass b1/b2 ≈ Janson's Δ, Poisson zero law) are measured: BRAINSTORM/s9_janson_dependency.md finds word-level Δ/μ = 3.6 → 9.4 over 108k primes ≤ 3·10⁶ (so any Poisson/TV bound from word-level dependency graphs is vacuous, μ²/2Δ ≈ 1–2 ≪ log p), level-granularity hits are critical (0.44→0.97·log p); BM_CORRECTED_COUNT §3.2 and BOARD2_SLATE show R/2 is ≈ swap-Poisson at moderate M but the far lower tail is fatter than Poisson; (★) is overdispersed 1.5–1.6×. Also any over-ℤ Poisson upper bound is false by T1 (squares), so only a BM-corrected over-primes version is conceivable — already discussed there.

Computed the bound: for fixed u, F(B,C) = 4uBC − u − B − p has W ≈ max(4uXY, p) ≈ p at the certificate scale XY ≈ p/(4u), so Coppersmith's integer bivariate condition XY < W^{2/3} holds iff u ≳ p^{1/3}/4, i.e. the Lenstra/CHN 'divisors of p+u in a class mod 4u > N^{1/3} (resp. N^{1/4})' regime. BRAINSTORM/s3_lll_lenstra.md already did exactly this (Lenstra 1984; Coppersmith–Howgrave-Graham–Nagaraj 2008; certificate census: 58% Lenstra-regime, 28% Coppersmith-only, 14% below N^{1/4}) and notes the decisive point: the reduced-basis norms depend only on the lattice determinant, not on whether a root exists (Minkowski short vector always exists), so lattice shortness cannot serve as an existence criterion; results are upper bounds (≤ 11 per line).

Did not install PySR (Julia); cheap stand-in: computed the minimal Type II e-slice e_min(p) for all 9732 primes p≡1 (24) < 10⁶ (mean 5.7, 53% have e_min=3, max 63 at p=87481) and regressed log e_min on log p and one-hot p mod primes ≤ 43: log p explains R²=0.002, residues R²=0.51 (held-out 0.47). So e_min is 'congruence profile × lottery', exactly the hardness_law.md / ident_invariants.md picture (half the variance local data, rest near-Poisson noise); there is no size law in log p for symbolic regression to find, and any formula it returns would be a congruence-class covering (B1).

BRAINSTORM/z45_program_synthesis.md already ran the non-LLM version of this loop: enumerative synthesis over 924 policies scored by solved primes and charged operations on all 9,732 primes p≡1 (24) ≤ 10⁶, held-out on 73,155 primes in (10⁶,10⁷]; the best policy (López line p+4..p+16, then forest parent scan) costs ≤ 1.118(log p)², but the factor-free parent-scan baseline already solves everything to 10⁷ with better tail, i.e. the search recovers a known line plus a moving-divisor fallback. An LLM proposer would only enlarge the policy space; the memo's selection result (no mechanism, cost ∝ (log p)² lottery) leaves no specific new hypothesis for FunSearch to test.
